one_line_contribution: That read-time verification of retrieved agent experience is authorship-dependent: the same scripted error planted in a trajectory the reader itself wrote is caught less often, and costs more downstream success, than when planted in another backbone's trajectory, with per-token NLL (familiarity) offered as the mediator via a self- vs cross-paraphrase 2x2 and a static external reference as the fix.
closest_prior_work: arXiv:2507.02778 (Self-Correction Bench, verified via s2cli, s2+hf, 16 citations) is the strongest threat and the proposal never cites it. It establishes exactly the reduced form the proposal calls its mechanism import: with error content held fixed, models correct errors injected into text presented as external but fail on the identical error in their own generation ('self-correction blind spot'), i.e. a detection asymmetry driven by authorship rather than by content, already demonstrated outside the self-preference/judge literature the proposal searched. Second: arXiv:2606.24428 (Escaping the Self-Confirmation Trap, verified, s2+hf) is built on the premise that a single agent misidentifies wrong-but-self-consistent trajectories as successful experience and that heterogeneous (non-self) verifiers fix it -- which is the proposal's C3 family and its D1 remedy, in the same setting (agentic experience learning), though it is a method paper that never crosses author x reader with content-identical planted errors. Third: arXiv:2608.00017 (Memory Reward Inflation, verified, s2+hf) names the 'Echo Gap' where self-graded rewards inflate incorrect episodes in retrieval-reused memory and prescribes 'error-independent verification'. None of these runs the reader x host-writer cross with one scripted edit rule held identical across writers, scores a reader-side detector by precision and recall against planted labels, or prices the defence on clean foreign items -- so the specific measurement survives -- but P2's headline result would read to an area chair as a domain transfer of a published effect, not a new mechanism, and the proposal's Related Work does not defend against that reading.
strongest_objection: The causal chain the title asserts -- detection failure causes the extra harm -- is powered nowhere. P5 compares self-host vs foreign-host per-retrieval loss in the rate {0,30,50%} cells, which run with NO detector at all; a larger loss on self-written hosts is fully explained by differential adoption (the reader imitates familiar text more, MemoryGraft 2512.16962's semantic imitation heuristic), with verification never in the loop. The only arms that could link detection to harm are the D0-gated 30% cells, at 2 seeds (about +-5 net), far too coarse for the difference-in-differences (gate benefit on self hosts minus on foreign hosts) that would actually test it. Second, the one prediction carrying the mechanism, P3(b), is underpowered by the proposal's own arithmetic (+5 margin against a +-4 half-width; the pre-review flags it unresolvable), and its qualification rule conditions on a post-treatment variable: self-paraphrases are admitted only if their NLL under the reader falls below the 75th percentile, so the analysed subset is selected on the very quantity whose effect is being estimated, while the cross-paraphrase comparator inherits that selection without satisfying it. If P3 does not resolve, what remains is P2 -- a recall gap that 2507.02778 already predicts -- plus P5, which admits an adoption explanation. Third, D1 'closing the gap' is close to arithmetic: gap_D1 = gap_D0 - self lift + foreign lift, so the >= 8 self-host lift clause largely delivers the <= 0.5 x gap clause unless D1 also lifts foreign hosts, and the gap clause is only scored when P2 already confirmed.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Put verification in the loop where harm is measured: run the gated arms at the rate that produces Gate-0 harm (50%, not only 30%) on both hosts at the Qwen3 reader's 6 seeds, and state the prediction as a difference-in-differences -- the gate recovers more success on self-written contamination than on foreign-written contamination -- so P5 tests detection rather than adoption. Add an adoption manipulation check (rate at which a retrieved planted action sequence is actually executed, by host) so the imitation explanation is separated from the verification explanation. (2) Fix P3: drop the 75th-percentile threshold and instead treat per-item reader NLL as a continuous mediator over all paraphrase pairs with a within-item regression (or stratify into pre-registered NLL bins), and either raise the arm to about 2,600 qualifying pairs or set clause (b)'s margin at >= 8, per the pre-review's own fix. (3) Cite and position against 2507.02778, 2606.24428 and 2608.00017 explicitly, and state what the agent-memory setting adds beyond them -- the honest answer is downstream success cost and the false-positive price of the defence, so lead with those rather than with P2. (4) Verify or drop the unverifiable 2605.22842.
missing_baseline: A cross-model verifier gate: have the other served backbone verify the reader's own store before acting. It is the deployable fix that both 2606.24428 (heterogeneous verifiers) and 2608.00017 ('error-independent verification') already advocate, both models are already served, and every item is already scored by both readers in the 2x2 -- yet no downstream cell gates with a foreign verifier, so the paper measures a failure whose obvious remedy it never prices against D0/D1. Reviewers will demand it precisely because the proposal's own framing implies it. Secondary omission (flagged by the pre-review and not addressed): a random-drop-and-refill placebo at the measured flag rate for P6, without which the gating cost on the clean mixed store is confounded with rank substitution rather than with the gate's decisions.
